original_question: While the cause of Gómez-López-Hernández syndrome is currently unknown, mutations in a gene on which chromosome have been implicated?

final_qi.question: While the cause of Gómez-López-Hernández syndrome is currently unknown, mutations in a gene on which chromosome have been implicated?
final_qi.long_answer: Although the etiology of Gómez-López-Hernández syndrome remains uncertain, several reports have described affected individuals carrying mutations or deletions involving the OTX2 homeobox gene, which is situated at 14q22-q23 on chromosome 14. This has led investigators to implicate chromosome 14 in the pathogenesis of the disorder.

0.question: Which gene mutations have been implicated in Gómez-López-Hernández syndrome?

final_answer.long_answer: Although Gómez-López-Hernández syndrome is still considered a disorder of unknown etiology, several patients who displayed the characteristic triad of rhombencephalosynapsis, trigeminal anaesthesia and parietal-occipital alopecia were found to harbour pathogenic variants in the PTF1A gene. PTF1A is located on chromosome 10p12; its disruption affects early hind-brain and cerebellar development, providing a plausible biological link to the cerebellar malformation seen in the syndrome. Consequently, mutations in this chromosome 10 gene have been implicated in the pathogenesis of Gómez-López-Hernández syndrome.
